photo.title: A full length oblique rear view portrait of a Bari girl standing in a homestead wearing an apron of metal chain links at the front, with a 'tail' of strings behind. She is also wearing a number of neck ornaments as well as metal wrist and ankle rings. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length full face portrait of a Bari girl standing in a homestead wearing an apron of metal chain links at the front, with a 'tail' of strings behind. She is also wearing a number of neck ornaments as well as metal wrist and ankle rings. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

An upper body full face portrait of a Bari girl sitting with hands together. She is wearing strings of beads around the neck and numerous short horizontal lines of cicatrices on her upper arms. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A group of three Bari men playing large and small hide-covered drums as well as a side-blown horn instrument. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

Several Bari men standing beside a homestead fence, one holding a parrying shield and spear. The Seligmans carried out investigations among the Bari of Belinian and Ali Bey in Jan 1922, before moving south to the Torit area among the Lotuko-speaking peoples.
A full length group postcard portrait of female and juvenile members of a Bari family standing in front of a hut.

A homestead grave in the village of Ali Bey, consisting of two notched stakes to which are tied a long peeled stick, and a sapling on which is hung pieces of slag. At the foot is a pot containing sacrifice, and also two groups of cooking stones, indicating two sacrifices have been made. The Seligmans carried out investigations among the Bari of Belinian and Ali Bey in Jan 1922, before moving south to the Torit area among the Lotuko-speaking people there.

A view down from the side of a steep hill, possibly Belinian, towards a Bari homestead, comprising a large and several smaller huts in a fenced compound. The Seligmans carried out investigations among the Bari of Belinian and Ali Bey in Jan 1922, before moving south to the Torit area among the Lotuko-speaking people there.

An upper body profile vignette portrait of a Bari man wearing a feather headdress and neck ornament, with cicatrice design on his shoulders, probably taken at Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length profile portrait of a Bari woman wearing a fringed skirt and arm and neck ornaments, standing in front of a hut entrance, probably at Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia. The hut door is unusual in that it seems to consist of a double door sealed by a large wooden latch, perhaps a chief's residence.

An upper body full face portrait of a seated Bari woman wearing a large belt of bead strings, tied together at the front. She is also wearing a large metal pendant around her neck as well as metal arm and wrist rings. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A Bari homestead in the foreground with the Nile and a rocky outcrop hill in the background, possibly Belinian hill. The homestead in the foreground comprises a large sleeping hut as well as a number of raised granaries. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length portrait of the Bari chief of Gondokoro named as Loron, standing in a fenced courtyard. It seems likely that this image was taken when Loron visited Lado to see Emin Pasha in Sept 1879 (see Felkin's account on page 86).

A posed group portrait of three Bari men, probably at Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia. The men have been posed so as to provide front, profile and rear views of Bari male decoration in the same image. Their ornamentation includes feather headdresses and animal fur arm ornaments.

An upper body profile portrait of a seated Bari woman wearing a large belt of bead strings, tied together at the front. She is also wearing a large metal pendant around her neck as well as metal arm and wrist rings. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

An upper body full face vignette portrait of a Bari man wearing a feather headdress and neck ornament, with cicatrice design on his shoulders, probably taken at Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length full face portrait of a Bari woman wearing a fringed skirt and arm and neck ornaments, standing in front of a hut entrance, probably at Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia. The hut door is unusual in that it seems to consist of a double door sealed by a large wooden latch, perhaps a chief's residence.

A full length profile portrait of a Bari woman wearing a fringed skirt at front and a hide apron behind. Around her waist is a belt consisting of strings of beads. She is standing in the same courtyard as that seen in an earlier image of the chief of Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length full face portrait of a Bari woman wearing a fringed skirt at front and a hide apron behind. Around her waist is a belt consisting of strings of beads. She is standing in the same courtyard as that seen in an earlier image of the chief of Gondokoro. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A full length portrait of a Bari man standing in front of a hut, holding a harp. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.
A photograph of an illustration (itself derived from an earlier photograph) of two Bari men, one working a bellows and the other cold-working metal against a stone.
A full length profile postcard portrait of a Bari mother with a goatskin baby carrier on her back with a baby inside.

An upper body profile portrait of a Bari girl sitting with hands together. She is wearing strings of beads around the neck and numerous short horizontal lines of cicatrices on her upper arm. It seems likely that this image was taken shortly before October 1878 when Buchta reached Lado (Juba) on board S.S. Safia.

A group of clay Bari pots gathered together on the ground. The Seligmans carried out investigations among the Bari of Belinian and Ali Bey in Jan 1922, before moving south to the Torit area among the Lotuko-speaking people there.

An old grind stone containing pieces of quartz and with old cooking stones nearby, marking the grave of the Belinian rain-maker's father. Next to the grave is an ebony post (feiti) which was notched near the top, a common feature of Bari graves. It is noted that the sacrifice for rain was undoubtedly carried out at this grave-shrine, when the rain stones held by the rain-maker were brought here to be anointed as part of a ceremony. The Seligmans carried out investigations among the Bari of Belinian and Ali Bey in Jan 1922, before moving south to the Torit area among the Lotuko-speaking people there.

An old grind stone containing a number of rain-making stones, marking the grave of the Bari rain-maker Jada, the great-grandfather of Ali Bey, the rain-maker met by the Seligmans in 1922. The grindstone contained four stones, one perforated, which they arranged on the side of the grindstone to photograph. They note that this grave was at the foot of Belinian hill, and that should rain fail and ceremonies at more recent rain-makers' graves not prove effective, then a ceremony would also be carried out at the grave of Jada.

A group portrait of two Bari (Fajelu) men with a woman between them in front of a hut. The man to the left has a quiver over his shoulder, bow and spears at his feet (one a large hunting spear). The man to the right has white feather hair decoration. The woman is wearing strings of beads around her neck. Buchta made an excursion to the groups west of the Nile in 1879 setting out from Juba on 7th July and returning there on 26th August.
An upper body full face postcard portrait of a Bari (Nyambara) girl with cicatrices on her abdomen and a lower lip ornament.
An upper body full face postcard portrait of a Bari (Fajelu) woman with dotted lines of cicatrices on her abdomen and forehead and a lower lip ornament, as well as a twisted metal neck ornament.

A full length full face postcard portrait of a Bari (Fajelu) woman with cicatrice designs on her abdomen and a pubic covering consisting of textile and fibre, with small bells at front. She is standing in front of a small granary.

Looking from the deck of a river boat towards a west-bank fishing settlement on the Nile, between Juba and Adok, possibly a Dinka settlement, or else one of the other groups living along that stretch of the Nile.
